fact: The Ministry of Home Affairs, through its civil registration department, runs the e-ID card application and issuing, including amendments and replacements.

The Office of the Prime Minister says it provides oversight, technology support, quality assurance and management of key components of the national population register on which the E-ID is built, and the Ministry of Home Affairs runs the existing registration infrastructure.
The Ministry of Home Affairs itself takes applications, prints and distributes national identity documents, printing 166,237 between 1 April 2025 and 30 June 2026, per its spokesperson.
